subject.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode — the roadmap

question: Should OpenClaw accept Codex-style structured questions, plan mode, and goal continuation as core runtime features now, and should the paired implementation be reviewed as one branch or split into staged PRs?
rationale: The request spans core runtime tools, Codex protocol bridging, gateway events, channel delivery, Control UI, config/default rollout, and unattended continuation semantics; that is a product and ownership decision rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Split staged PRs
options.body: Keep this hub open and ask for separate question-pipeline, plan-mode, and goal-driver review paths with focused proof for each surface.

options.title: Sponsor broad branch
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the combined review cost and require the paired PR to clear its SDK, approval, upgrade, security, and live-channel proof blockers before merge.

options.title: Defer or narrow
options.body: Maintainers can reject or narrow the roadmap if some primitives should wait for a smaller plugin/API design or a later core rollout.

recommendation.title: Split staged PRs
recommendation.body: Keep this hub open and ask for separate question-pipeline, plan-mode, and goal-driver review paths with focused proof for each surface.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the adjacent execution-contract, update_plan, and session-goal behavior that this roadmap would change by default.
